mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday foot traffic and spillover shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -73.4 to -64.7 over the last three weekly means
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays flat or falls and RETAIL_REC is still lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM indicates households are making more essential trips and combining errands, which then lifts nearby retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 10 points from the prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -54.9 to -35.1 before easing to -36.6
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses the stated threshold and RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, commute-linked passing traffic and lunch-time shopping rise, producing a higher RETAIL_REC level over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -84.1 to -68.9 while WORKPLACES improved from -72.6 to -64.7
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 25 points while TRANSIT remains below -65, stay-at-home behavior suppresses discretionary shopping and RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 25 and TRANSIT < -65 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is about 28 while TRANSIT remains around -71
failure_condition: If the stated residential-transit regime persists and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly rebound in PARKS mobility signals better weather and more outdoor leisure, which should pull retail-and-recreation mobility upward within one week through broader out-of-home activity.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -74.7 to -36.7 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS shows a one-week jump of at least 15 points and RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM weakens while RESIDENTIAL stays high, households consolidate trips and avoid discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -40 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 25
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is near -36.6 and RESIDENTIAL is near 28.0
failure_condition: If grocery mobility weakens under the stated residential constraint and RETAIL_REC does not drop within 14 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in TRANSIT after severe suppression marks reopening of shared mobility and supports shopping access, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 10 points from its prior weekly mean and stays above -75
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -84.1 and -82.4 up to -68.9 before easing to -70.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT meets the trigger but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT signals broader return of discretionary travel, and that combination should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT both improved sharply between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT recover together but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week average over the next 28 days, the interaction hypothesis fails.
